name: nonApi_syncMemberStandingBit
description: Single maintenance point for the AUTOMATED MEMBER bit (0x0001) of one HC.HasherKennelMap row's KennelStanding: sets the bit when the user's membership is current (MembershipExpirationDate >= now), clears it when lapsed or absent. Never touches the manual bits (ALUMNI 0x0002, TRUSTED 0x0004, ADMIN 0x0100). Called (EXEC) by every SP that writes MembershipExpirationDate; the row-wise equivalent of nonApi_sweepMemberStanding. No-op when the bit is already right, which avoids a pointless updatedAt restamp; when it does write, the HKM trigger restamps updatedAt and the row re-syncs. Internal; no auth. Returns nothing; a runtime error is logged to HC.ErrorLog and re-thrown into the caller.

parameters.name: userId
parameters.description: The hasher of the HKM row to sync.

parameters.name: kennelId
parameters.description: The kennel of the HKM row to sync.

sideEffects: UPDATE HC.HasherKennelMap SET KennelStanding (bit 0x0001 only) WHERE UserId = @userId AND KennelId = @kennelId AND the result differs — the HKM trigger restamps updatedAt when it writes.
On any runtime error: rolls back if a transaction is open (it usually runs inside the caller's), inserts one HC.ErrorLog row (HcVersion '<unknown>'), then THROWs.

codeSmells.detail: @userId, @kennelId have no SQL default. Called only by EXEC from the membership-writing SPs, which pass both. A call that omits one fails before the body runs — no HC.ErrorLog row, no graceful check (CLAUDE.md 'SP parameter with NO default').

codeSmells.issue: GETDATE() (server local DATETIME) compared with a DATETIMEOFFSET(7) column
codeSmells.detail: Lines 26 and 34 compare MembershipExpirationDate (an instant) with GETDATE(), which is implicitly converted with the server offset. Right on Azure SQL (UTC clock) but SYSDATETIMEOFFSET() says what is meant; kept identical to nonApi_sweepMemberStanding so the two agree.

codeSmells.issue: CATCH rolls back the CALLER's transaction before logging
codeSmells.detail: Line 40: IF @@TRANCOUNT > 0 ROLLBACK TRANSACTION. This SP opens no transaction of its own, so when it is EXECed inside a caller's transaction (its normal use) an error here rolls back the caller's whole unit of work and leaves @@TRANCOUNT = 0 — the caller's own COMMIT/ROLLBACK then raises 'no corresponding BEGIN TRANSACTION'. The THROW reaches the caller's CATCH either way, so nothing is lost, but the rollback belongs to the caller.

breakingChangeRules: Never remove a column from any rowset
Never change a sentinel value meaning
Never change errorType integer codes without updating all callers
